transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-18
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Reed (Redwood SE), Ava Martinez (HeliosPay CTO), Priya Singh (Infra Eng), Liam O'Connor (ML Eng)

Summary:
Quick pilot sync to review this week's latency runs (TTFT and streaming behavior), triage sequence-length tail, and plan the handoff for private deployment requirements. Decent improvements on mid-tail with new kernel combo but microburst P95 spikes remain. Action items around additional sampling and seqlen histogram from customer.

Topics covered:
- Recent TTFT numbers (p50/p95) for streaming vs non-streaming paths
- Effects of capping sequence length and prompt segmentation
- Kernel selection tradeoffs (vectorized vs tiled kernels)
- KV cache behavior and prefix caching regressions
- Next steps for a private/VPC feasibility pass and security doc share

Action items (recorded here for the meeting):
- Maya: Share pricing + benchmark sheet
- Jonah: Run microburst trace with KV cache disabled, include perf logs
- Priya: Provide production token length histogram and traffic percentiles

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. We wanted to cover the latest TTFT runs and decide whether to push the new kernel combo to the pilot nodes or keep the hedge in place.
[00:00:19] Ava (HeliosPay CTO): Thanks Maya. Quick context — our SLO is 120ms p95 TTFT for card auth interactive flows. Last week you folks showed 90ms p95 on hosted but we saw 170ms in our test cluster, so trying to reconcile.
[00:00:35] Jonah (Redwood SE): Right, the 90ms was using streaming + early-token path with the tiled-attn kernel and aggressive batching heuristics. On your pilot cluster we think the default routing ended up on the vectorized kernel which increases per-token latency in some microburst patterns.
[00:00:50] Priya (HeliosPay Infra Eng): yeah that sounds like what we saw — spikes when a batch from a sudden burst hits the vectorized path, we had a queueing jitter that amplified it.
[00:01:05] Liam (HeliosPay ML Eng): Quick note: our average sequence length is 120 but we have a long tail up to 2,000 tokens on error investigation prompts. Most of our auth path is short but the diagnostic path is long.
[00:01:22] Maya: That sequence tail is probably the main factor. Jonah, can you summarize the seqlen capping experiments you ran?
[00:01:34] Jonah: Sure. We did three runs: baseline (no cap), cap@512, cap@384. Each run used streaming enabled and prefix KV caching. Results — baseline p95 was 165ms on your infra, cap@512 dropped to 140ms, cap@384 hit 112ms p95 but we noticed a small regression in some generated completions when prompts were clipped.
[00:01:58] Ava: "small regression" — can you quantify? For auth flows we can clip but diagnostics we cannot.
[00:02:06] Jonah: Mostly partial sentences at the end of long responses, sometimes missing closing tokens. We ran a quality eval on 500 examples: cap@384 had a delta of 0.8%QA-drop on the auth rubric, but on the diagnostics set the drop was 4.6%.
[00:02:28] Priya: From infra perspective, the cap@384 looked attractive for our main path. But we need a safe fallback for diagnostics.
[00:02:36] Maya: Agreed. One option is routing: short auth requests get the trimmed path + tiled kernel, long diagnostics go to a lower-priority lane or to hosted variant. That keeps SLOs for auth while preserving quality for diagnostics.
[00:02:52] Ava: Routing is fine but we need to understand the operational cost — if we send diagnostics to hosted, whats the egress / per-token cost?
[00:03:01] Maya: We'll surface that in the pricing sheet; rough numbers shown in the benchmark indicate about 1.8x per-token cost on hosted when compared to dedciated quantized variants — sorry "dedicated" variants. We'll put actual per-token numbers in the doc.
[00:03:15] Liam: Also, the KV cache seems to cause higher p95 when cold. We saw particular microbursts when a cache miss causes a backend hop.
[00:03:25] Jonah: Yeah, microburst behavior — there's a cold-cache penalty and also the cache lookup path in the current infra has a small head-of-line blocking in the vectorized kernel. Disabling KV cache for auth (short-seq) flows actually reduced p95 in our stress tests.
[00:03:40] Priya: Interesting — can you repeat that under our trace generator? We can flip KV cache off for the auth route and run a 10k user replay.
[00:03:48] Jonah: We can. We'll also attach logs that show the per-token timing break down — prefix lookup, kernel exec, serialization.
[00:03:55] Speaker 2 (transcriber): [mumbling] prefix look up transcribed as K V catch at 03:40, sorry for the noise.
[00:04:05] Ava: No worries. On kernel choices, can you explain the tiled vs vectorized trade-offs again in plain terms?
[00:04:12] Jonah: Tiled-attn is optimized for short sequences with better memory locality; it wins when seq < ~512 and under streaming because it reduces kernel launch overhead. Vectorized kernels are better for large batch or long sequences; they amortize per-token cost but can be worse for low-latency single-request bursts.
[00:04:33] Maya: And the new kernel combo we tested last week mixes tiled for the first N layers and vectorized for later layers — we saw stable p50 improvements and some p95 wins, but on your infra the microburst pattern favored vectorized fallback and spiked.
[00:04:49] Ava: Is that fallback automatic? Could we force the tiled path for auth?
[00:04:54] Jonah: Yes it's policy driven. We can hard pin the tiled path for requests with a request tag or route key. That will avoid the fallback but slightly reduce throughput for batch workloads.
[00:05:07] Liam: Throughput hit is acceptable for auth, since auth is short lived and low compute overall. Our concern is throughput for bulk billing jobs later.
[00:05:16] Maya: So short-term plan: cap auth at 384 and pin tiled kernel; route diagnostics to hosted or dedicated flagged instance that supports vectorized. Jonah will run more microburst replays to confirm.
[00:05:28] Priya: We also need to check TLS termination and KMS integration for private mode. If we move to VPC/private, we'll need to ensure our HSM policies plus audit log retention meet compliance.
[00:05:39] Maya: We'll include the security doc in the share. Our Private offering supports KMS integrations and audit logs; Jonah can walk through the options on next demo.
[00:05:48] Ava: Great. Quick note: we observed occasional tokenization mismatch between your tokenizer and our pre-tokenizer — small differences that can push token counts higher. Any way to normalize?
[00:05:59] Jonah: We can provide a tokenizer spec and a docker image for pre-tokenization so you can run parity tests. Also we'll include a sample script to compute token counts from your logs.
[00:06:10] Speaker 1 (system): [00:06:10] transcription glitch — "pre-tokenizer" transcribed as "pre taco nizer" in some segments.
[00:06:20] Liam: One question on streaming handshake — we saw about 12ms added latency on the first WS frame. Is that in your measurements too?
[00:06:28] Jonah: There's a small handshake overhead especially when we force low-latency batching. On our infra it's about 8-14ms depending on network. We can shave some by keeping persistent streams or reusing connections.
[00:06:39] Priya: Persistent streams look doable but we need to ensure connection churn doesn't exceed our LB timeouts. We'll run a config test.
[00:06:46] Maya: OK. For the microburst tests Jonah — when you run with KV off can you also try cap@384 and tiled-pinned? That's our recommended auth path.
[00:06:55] Jonah: Yes. We'll do four runs: baseline, cap384+tiled, cap384+tiled+KV-off, and cap384+hosted-diagnostics-routing. We'll include p50/p95/p99 and a sample of 200 traces.
[00:07:09] Ava: Sounds good. How long will that take?
[00:07:12] Jonah: We can run and deliver results within 36 hours if we have your traffic replay file.
[00:07:18] Priya: We'll push a sanitized replay to the shared bucket today. ETA for us is EOD.
[00:07:23] Maya: Perfect. On pricing — quick note, dedicated quantized nodes give best per-token cost but require a 3-month reservation for predictable throughput. We'll outline options in the sheet.
[00:07:34] Liam: Can you include an amortized cost per 1M auth requests? That helps us model.
[00:07:38] Maya: Yes. We'll include a model for amortized cost at different commit levels.
[00:07:42] Ava: One last topic — rollout strategy. If we pin tiled for auth, what's the fallback if tiled kernel degrades after a push?
[00:07:51] Jonah: We recommend a canary: route 5% auth traffic to the new kernel combo for 24 hours, monitor TTFT and error rates, then roll to 25% and so on. Automatic fallback policy can move traffic back to the previous variant if p95 crosses threshold.
[00:08:05] Priya: We'll want the circuit breaker thresholds documented.
[00:08:08] Maya: We'll add those thresholds to the rollout plan in the doc.
[00:08:12] Speaker 2: [murmur] note about canary percentages.
[00:08:20] Jonah: Also, regarding your long-diagnostic prompts — we can implement prompt chunking with reconstruction to avoid clipping while still keeping the auth path short; it adds a small post-processing cost but keeps quality.
[00:08:34] Liam: That might work, can you prototype chunking with our sample diagnostics set?
[00:08:38] Jonah: Yes — I'll include a small prototype script in the run artifacts.
[00:08:43] Ava: Ok, recap please?
[00:08:45] Maya: Recap: 1) Jonah runs the four microburst experiments with KV off/ on and cap@384 pinned to tiled; 2) HeliosPay uploads replay and seqlen histogram (Priya) by tomorrow; 3) Redwood shares pricing + benchmarks by 2027-01-20; 4) Schedule private deployment feasibility demo for 2027-01-25.
[00:09:06] Priya: Correct. We'll also add our LB timeout configs to the shared bucket.
[00:09:10] Maya: Great. Anything else from the group?
[00:09:13] Ava: One small ask — include an appendix with failure-mode examples for the tiled vs vector kernels. That helps our SRE oncall read through.
[00:09:22] Jonah: Will do.
[00:09:24] Liam: Also please include a note on tokenization parity and provide the docker tokenizer image.
[00:09:30] Maya: Noted.
[00:09:32] Speaker 1: [background: dog barking briefly] sorry for the noise.
[00:09:40] Maya: Alright thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the doc and reconvene after Jonah posts the runs.
[00:09:46] Ava: Thanks.
[00:09:47] Priya: Thanks all.
[00:09:48] Jonah: Thanks.
[00:55:00] Meeting end (call disconnected).

Notes on transcription: there are a few mis-heard tokens and some speaker switches where the export labeled speaker generically. Technical terms occasionally rendered oddly (e.g., "K V catch" for KV cache, "pre taco nizer" for pre-tokenizer). These are preserved to reflect raw transcript feel.
